title.value: Myeloarchitecture gradients in the human insula: Histological underpinnings and association to intrinsic functional connectivity
title.justification: The title is clearly stated at the very beginning of the paper under the 'journal homepage.'
title.quote: Myeloarchitecture gradients in the human insula: Histological underpinnings and association to intrinsic functional connectivity

analysis.description: The paper investigates the myeloarchitecture of the human insular cortex, examining its histological structure and its association with intrinsic functional connectivity patterns. Using MRI data and histological analysis, the study identifies principal gradients in myeloarchitectural differentiation correlating with functional systems in the brain.

type.justification: The study involves comprehensive data collection and analysis using high-resolution MRI and post mortem histological data, making it an empirical research study.
type.quote: We studied 109 unrelated adults (62 women, 28.5 3.7 years) from the S900 release of the Human Connectome Project initiative...

name.justification: The paper focuses on the structure and function of the human insular cortex, which falls under the domain of neuroscience.
name.quote: Insular cortex is a core hub involved in multiple cognitive and socio-affective processes.

name.justification: The study utilizes MRI techniques to map myeloarchitectural gradients in the human insular cortex.
name.quote: Advances in high-field magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) allow neuroanatomical approaches to be extended to describe brain microstructure in vivo.

name.justification: The paper examines the relationship between myeloarchitectural gradients and intrinsic functional connectivity in the brain.
name.quote: Resting-state functional connectomics in the same individuals and ad hoc meta-analyses showed that myelin gradients in the insula relate to diverse affiliation to macroscale intrinsic functional systems.

name.justification: The study uses data from the Human Connectome Project, which provides the MRI and surface models for analysis.
name.quote: We studied 109 unrelated adults (62 women, 28.5 3.7 years) from the S900 release of the Human Connectome Project initiative, HCP (Glasser et al., 2013; Van Essen et al., 2013).

referenced_paper_title.value: The Wu-Minn human connectome project: an overview.
referenced_paper_title.justification: The paper cites this study as a reference for the Human Connectome Project dataset.
referenced_paper_title.quote: Consortium, W.-M.H.C.P., 2013. The Wu-Minn human connectome project: an overview. Neuroimage 80, 62–79.

name.justification: The study utilizes data from the BigBrain project for histological analysis of brain specimens.
name.quote: Histological data acquisition and preprocessing. A high-resolution Merker-stained 3D volumetric histological reconstruction of a post mortem human brain from a 65-year-old male was obtained from the open-access BigBrain repository (https://bigbrain.loris.ca/main.php) (Amunts et al., 2013).

referenced_paper_title.value: BigBrain: an ultrahigh-resolution 3D human brain model.
referenced_paper_title.justification: The paper cites this reference when describing the histological data obtained from the BigBrain repository.
referenced_paper_title.quote: Amunts, K., Lepage, C., Borgeat, L., et al., 2013. BigBrain: an ultrahigh-resolution 3D human brain model. Science 340 (80), 1472–1475.

name.justification: The BrainSpace toolbox is used for gradient mapping in the analysis of microstructural gradients.
name.quote: Gradient mapping. Microstructural gradients in the insula were identified with the BrainSpace toolbox for Matlab (https://github.com/MICA-MNI/BrainSpace) (Vos de Wael et al., 2020).

referenced_paper_title.value: BrainSpace: a toolbox for the analysis of macroscale gradients in neuroimaging and connectomics datasets.
referenced_paper_title.justification: The paper cites this reference for the BrainSpace toolbox used in the study.
referenced_paper_title.quote: Vos de Wael, R., Benkarim, O., Paquola, C., Lariviere, S., Royer, J., Tavakol, S., Xu, T., Hong, S.-J., Langs, G., Valk, S., Misic, B., Milham, M., Margulies, D., Smallwood, J., Bernhardt, B.C., 2020. BrainSpace: a toolbox for the analysis of macroscale gradients in neuroimaging and connectomics datasets. Commun. Biol. 3, 103.

name.justification: FreeSurfer is used for cortical surface extractions in the study.
name.quote: Image preprocessing. Cortical surfaces were extracted from T1w images using FreeSurfer 6.0 (Dale et al., 1999; Fischl et al., 1999a, 1999b).
